description: 4 should-trigger + 3 should-not-trigger. Should-trigger covers branch naming, commit message conventions, PR creation and the push-settle loop, including a German phrasing that never names Git. Should-not-trigger covers near-miss neighbors: rewriting already-pushed history (git-history-discipline), a destructive reset/force-push (non-destructive-by-default), and a merge-conflict resolution strategy question that belongs to a different command.

queries.q: push this branch and open a PR
what commit message format does this repo use?
wie soll der Branch heißen und wie schreibe ich die Commit-Message?
rebase the last three commits and squash them into one, already pushed
queries.note: rewriting published history is git-history-discipline's territory, not this skill's naming/PR-flow scope

queries.q: force-push over the remote branch to discard what's there
queries.note: a destructive history operation gated by non-destructive-by-default, not a workflow-convention question

queries.q: I have a merge conflict, which approach should I take to resolve it?
queries.note: conflict-resolution strategy belongs to /pr:merge's enumerated classes, not git-workflow's conventions
